- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or lagging in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecast accuracy improves when model adjusts downward after a peak, but often lags by 1–3 days.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true values show a downward trend.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model tends to overreact and forecast higher than true outcome.
- Model is sensitive to recent volatility — if last 5 days show high variance, forecast tends to be more erratic and less accurate.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in the last 10 days — tends to hold high forecasts even when true values are declining.
